rule: The square mosaic is mirror symmetric about off-centre axes: column x mirrors to S+1-x and row y to S+1-y (31-x and 31-y at native size 30). Colour-9 blobs hide cells. Step 1 fills each 9 from any visible horizontal, vertical or point mirror partner. Step 2 fills any remaining 9 from its transpose partner (x,y) or that partner's mirror images, read on the step-1 canvas. Those partners must agree on exactly one value.
scope: Supported: even square sizes 16..30. Native 30 is sampled 60% of the time; the other sizes are synthetic extensions keeping the same two-cell off-centre crop. Pure H/V repair scenes (about 65% of default draws), and diagonal-fallback scenes from four latent occluder families. These are edge blocks straddling the seam (native test case), shadow (the plain transpose is hidden in the input but restored in step 1), interior four-fold orbits, and a corner-strip probe. H/V distractor rectangles include three-of-four mirror orbits that force point-mirror recovery. Explicit quadrant/masks/size/palette/diagonal/family controls are honoured or rejected with ValueError. Not supported: odd sizes, non-square grids, occluder colours other than 9, mosaics with no hidden-cell recoverability, and scenes where a nearer-centre axis stays consistent.

known_limitations: Only one native example (the test) exercises the diagonal fallback. The left-edge, shadow, orbit, strip and non-30 variants are synthetic extensions consistent with the archived rule, not native coverage.
The strip family is a minimal corner probe with exactly one fallback cell, (0,1) or (1,0). No richer corner case is possible, because (0,0) and (1,1) are their own transposes.
Axis refutation is achieved by rejection sampling, not by planting. With 2-colour palettes at size 16 the success rate is believed high but has not been measured.
Overlapping distractor rectangles merge into irregular blobs, as in native train 2. This is intended.
Fixture quadrants were transcribed from canonical outputs. They are reconstructed only through explicit generate(quadrant=..., masks=...) calls.
Bounded solver agreement and control checks do not prove complete coverage of every interpretation of the task.

authored_constraints: Output equals the rendering of the latent quadrant and contains only colours 1..8; input differs only at cells set to 9.
Every hidden cell is either H/V/point-mirror recoverable from a visible cell, or has at least one diagonal partner known on the step-1 canvas.
All known diagonal partners of fallback cells agree with the true colour; this is enforced by equalising the quadrant transpose pair each fallback cell reads.
Axes size/2 and size/2-1 (centre and tie-winning candidate) are refuted by visible cells both vertically and horizontally, so the rule picks axis size/2+1.
In diagonal mode at least one hidden cell needs the fallback; with diagonal=False none does.
Hidden cell count is between 3 and size*size/4; all mask rectangles lie in bounds.
